assumptions.choice: Use the signal bar's close as the entry-price estimate when computing R, SL, TP, and share size at signal time; the actual fill (next bar open, backtrader default) is only used to set the recorded entry_price in notify_order.
assumptions.reason: Spec gives no explicit fill-timing rule; exact next-bar fill price is unknown at the moment the signal fires.

assumptions.choice: For each of the three levels (38.2/50/61.8% of R), treat a bar as a 'bounce at that zone' if the bar's Low (long) / High (short) reaches at or beyond the level intrabar while the Close finishes back on the breakout side of that same level.
assumptions.reason: Spec names three specific percentage levels but does not define a tolerance band; touch-and-close-back is the most literal reading of 'pullback to a Fib zone ... closes with a bounce'.

assumptions.topic: 1 signal per direction / max 2 trades per day
assumptions.choice: Cap each direction (long, short) at one executed trade per day, and additionally gate execution to one 'morning' (London) slot and one 'day' (New York) slot, each usable once.
assumptions.reason: Reconciles the two stated caps ('1 per direction per day' and 'max 2: one morning, one day') into a single consistent rule.

assumptions.choice: Treat as a whole-day gate: if neither ORH nor ORL has been broken by 12:00, disable both the morning and afternoon trade for that entire day.
assumptions.reason: Spec states the rule once, not per-direction; a day-level gate is the most literal reading.

assumptions.choice: No new entry evaluation (breakout/pullback/trigger scanning) occurs between 12:00 and 13:30; the London and New York windows are the only times entries are scanned/submitted.
assumptions.reason: Spec defines only 'morning until 12:00' and 'after 13:30' as the two trading windows, implying a pause between them.

assumptions.choice: Enabled by default (not behind an extra toggle) with multiplier 1.25 (midpoint of the stated 1.0-1.5 range); once profit exceeds 1.0xR it takes over as the exit mechanism ahead of the static take-profit, in addition to the always-active stop-loss and timeout.
assumptions.reason: Spec presents ATR trailing as a defined feature of position management ('Optional trailing: when profit > 1.0xR, enable...') rather than a user flag, so it is applied whenever its stated condition is met.

assumptions.topic: New-York 'patient' trade after a morning loss
assumptions.choice: Force TP = 1.5xR (ignore Q-based sizing) for the day trade when the morning trade closed at a loss; rely on the already-generalized 1.0xR trailing-stop rule to satisfy 'hold until timeout with trailing enabled'.
assumptions.reason: Spec's two bullet points for this case restate the base TP-floor and base trailing behavior together; no additional distinct mechanism is described.

assumptions.choice: Session open 09:30, market close 16:00 (standard US equity hours) used to derive the 30-minute pre-close timeout cutoff (15:30), even though the supplied 5-minute feed's last bar is 15:55; London = OR-window-end to 12:00; New York = 13:30 to 15:30 for new entries (15:30-15:55 only manages/times-out existing positions).
assumptions.reason: Spec references market close and session windows but the feed only contains intraday bars; 16:00 is the conventional US market close and is needed to compute the stated 30-minute timeout offset.

assumptions.choice: Evaluate R < k*ATR(14) once, on the first bar after the OR window closes, using that bar's ATR(14) value; if triggered, skip the entire day (no morning or day trade).
assumptions.reason: Spec gives the rule but not an evaluation point; checking immediately once R is known is the most literal placement.

assumptions.choice: 'BB width increasing vs previous bar' and 'EMA slope aligned' are computed as strict one-bar-over-previous-bar comparisons (index 0 vs index -1).
assumptions.reason: Spec states both as bar-over-bar comparisons without further smoothing.

assumptions.choice: 'Equity' in the position-size formula is self.broker.getvalue() (total account equity) evaluated at signal time; size is floored to a whole number of shares via int() truncation.
assumptions.reason: Ensures risk never exceeds the stated X% cap ('no more than X%'), consistent with the spec's rounding instruction.

assumptions.choice: Rely on backtrader's automatic minperiod (canonical default) with no manual bar-skipping; consequently next() is first invoked only once all indicators (longest: EMA(21), needs 21 bars) are warmed up, which falls after the first day's OR window closes, so day 1's High/Low are never accumulated and day 1 is skipped entirely by the existing 'OR data missing -> day disabled' path.
assumptions.reason: The environment's fixed automatic-minperiod behavior and the prohibition on manual bar-skipping make full OR capture on the very first trading day impossible without violating the canonical default; all subsequent days are unaffected since indicators are already warm.
